long_biography.plain_text:
Zanetti entered the coffee industry in 1973 by acquiring the Segafredo roasting plant near Bologna. He revitalised the operating business, attached his name to the brand and used it as the base for an international expansion. Growth came through new markets, vertical integration and purchases of additional roasting and distribution companies.

The resulting Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group later entered the Milan market, then returned to private ownership after a takeover led through Zanetti-controlled holding structures. In 2024, QuattroR acquired half of the company and installed Pierluigi Tosato as chief executive. Zanetti remained founder and chairman, while his family retained a substantial block. Subsequent reporting places that family position below half and gives the investment partner board and voting control. This makes the ownership boundary important: the family stake is not automatically Zanetti's individual stake, and group revenue, brands, plants, debt or valuations are corporate measures. His retained position remains tied to the coffee group, but current daily management belongs to the chief executive.
